eps_directives.directive:
This chapter carries the arc's highest emotional load. Work the full analysis before drafting a line.
Resolve every zero-subject sentence to a named speaker and referent — at this temperature a mis-attributed line rewrites the scene. Track where the register breaks: a character losing composure under pressure is a source-marked event, not noise to smooth. Honor it.
Run the kanji perception pass at full attention. Marked items are dense here — authors reach for graph-versus-reading gaps precisely at emotional peaks. Where a passage moves into classical, epistolary, or verse register, adopt the 信達雅 frame: accuracy first, then fluency, then formal beauty, in that order and never inverted. Elegance that costs accuracy is a failure, not a flourish.
Where an effect cannot survive into English, say so in your analysis rather than inventing an English effect that was never in the source. Silence is preferable to compensation the author did not earn.

Elevated register, active emotional current, but not the arc's peak.
Resolve speaker and referent for every ambiguous sentence. Attend to interpersonal distance — 敬語 tier, address forms, and the direction any shift is travelling. Movement between registers is usually the scene's actual content.
Run the kanji perception pass. Mark and analyze genuine marked items; pass over conventional orthography without comment. A thorough reading of this chapter is one that catches every marked item — not one that finds a marked item in every line.

Baseline narrative. Standard analytical posture, no reduction in rigor.
Resolve speaker and referent. Hold voice separation across the active cast — the quiet chapters are where distinct voices silently converge into one narrator, and the drift is invisible until several chapters later. That convergence is the real risk in this band, and it is worth the whole of your attention.
Run the kanji perception pass at normal attention. Most orthography here is conventional; treat it as such and move on.

Expository, transitional, or procedural material. Translate cleanly and directly.
Two-Step posture: render the source faithfully, then read your own English once for naturalness and fix what reads as translated. Do not manufacture literary weight the passage does not carry — over-elevating flat exposition is a defect, not care.
Thoroughness in this band means verifying accuracy, not discovering depth. Direct it at referents, terminology locks, tense, and continuity with prior chapters. A scrupulous reading of expository prose still concludes that the prose is expository.
Kanji perception applies to register stratum only. Do not hunt for marked items in routine prose; conventional orthography is read for meaning and passed over.

Minimal emotional load — logistics, recap, scene-setting, mechanical description.
Two-Step posture. Accuracy and clarity are the whole job. Keep locked terminology exact and keep the prose out of the way.
Attention here belongs to precision — names, numbers, times, places, referents, locked terms, agreement with what earlier chapters established. It does not belong to interpretation. Finding nothing to interpret in a COLD chapter is the correct result, and reporting that plainly is the correct analysis.
Kanji perception applies to register stratum only. Finding significance in ordinary orthography here is a failure mode, not diligence — a COLD chapter rendered with HOT-band ornament reads as deliberate craft and survives review, which makes it worse than flatness, not better.
